subject: Evaluation plan & usage headroom — clarifying overage / burst terms
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlasretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 21:03:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation plan & usage headroom during POC

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Before we lock the POC dates, procurement asked for a short note on how Redwood handles overages and short-term bursts during the ramp. Specifically:

- If we commit to a monthly baseline for Q3 but exceed it during a short marketing surge, how are overages billed?
- Can we get a temporary usage cap so we don’t accidentally spike costs during the POC?
- If we move from evaluation to a committed reserved plan mid-quarter, how are credits/ramps reconciled?

We want to build this into our MAP so legal/procurement have clear expectations. Can you provide a short write-up we can attach to the MAP and share with procurement?

Appreciate it —
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, AI Product
Atlas Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & usage headroom during POC

Hi Liam —

Great questions. I drafted the short note below and attached a proposed MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) and our current rate card (Redwood_Ratecard_Q3.pdf). High level summary first, then specific clauses you can drop into the MAP:

Summary (TL;DR)
- Short-term bursts above committed baseline are billed at the standard overage rate in our rate card, with a capped "burst premium" that only applies to the burst volume above the burst threshold.
- During a POC/evaluation we can apply a temporary soft cap to alert and throttle at a level you define; hard caps require mutual agreement and may affect quality/degraded fallback behavior.
- If you convert mid-quarter to a reserved/committed plan, usage above the new committed baseline that occurred before signing is credited toward the first billing period per the ramp credit terms in the MAP.

Suggested MAP clause (for procurement/legal)
- Baseline Commitment: Customer commits to a baseline monthly token/embedding usage of X units.
- Burst Threshold: For each month, a burst threshold equal to 120% of baseline will be allowed; usage between 100% and 120% billed at the standard overage rate. Usage above 120% billed at the burst premium rate (see rate card).
- Soft Caps & Alerts: During the evaluation phase Redwood will enable usage alerts at the customer-defined threshold and offer optional request throttling to prevent runaway costs.
- Mid-Quarter Conversion: If Customer upgrades to a Reserved plan mid-quarter, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to the billed overage charges from the first day of the billing period up to the conversion effective date, capped at the committed level of the first reserved month.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (proposed milestones & payment schedule), Redwood_Ratecard_Q3.pdf (rates and definitions).

Rishi — can you confirm the exact numeric multipliers for "burst premium" and whether we can offer a one-month waiver on the first burst during POC? Grace — can you add the MAP milestones (evaluation tasks, success criteria, sign-offs) to sheet 2 and mark expected dates?

Next steps: I can circulate a single-page summary for procurement that they can include in the MAP if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & usage headroom during POC

Adding the technical/pricing clarity requested. Short version then examples.

Pricing mechanics
- Standard overage: billed per-token at the standard pay-as-you-go rate in Redwood_Ratecard_Q3.pdf.
- Burst premium: applied only to volume above the burst threshold (120% of baseline in Marissa's suggested clause). For Atlas we can set burst premium = 1.5x the standard overage rate for the portion above 120%.
- Waiver: For the evaluation period we can offer a one-time waiver of burst premium for the first month (Atlas only) if the MAP milestones for Phase 1 are met by the sign-off date. Overage charges at standard rate would still apply.

Usage caps & protection
- Soft cap (recommended): Alerts at 80%/100%/110% of baseline with email + Slack notifications to your ops distribution.
- Hard cap (optional): Stops processing beyond the hard cap. Requires a signed change order; may result in degraded results if models are throttled.

Practical examples (numbers for clarity)
- Baseline = 10 million token-equivalents/month.
- 0–10M: included in baseline/commit.
- 10M–12M (100–120%): billed at standard overage = $0.0008/token.
- >12M: billed at burst premium = $0.0012/token (1.5x).

Mid-quarter conversion example
- If Atlas signs reserved plan on 2025-07-20 and the new baseline is 30M/month: overages from 2025-07-01 through 2025-07-19 that would have been covered by the new baseline are credited up to the new baseline for month 1, not exceeding the invoiced overage amount.

I attached a CSV with a sample breakdown (burst_pricing_example.csv) and a one-page note we can hand to procurement.

If you want different multipliers (e.g., 1.25x vs 1.5x) we can flex depending on commit size/term.

Rishi
Head of Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlasretail.com>

Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & usage headroom during POC

Marissa/Rishi — thanks, this is exactly what procurement needed. Two quick asks before we finalize the MAP doc: 

1) Procurement wants the burst premium clause to explicitly call out the calculation and that credits (from mid-quarter conversion) apply before any refunds — i.e., we agree credits reduce the next invoice rather than a separate reimbursement.
2) They asked if Redwood can pre-configure the soft alerts and a default soft cap at 150% of baseline for the POC, and then we can reduce it to 120% for production. That helps Ops avoid surprise spikes during the marketing push.

If you can confirm both items I will route the revised MAP to legal. Also send the DocuSign link and the HubSpot deal update when you have the final file.

Thanks —
Liam
